transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess I came in because I’ve just had this kind of heavy, flat feeling for a long time. It’s not like things are terrible, exactly—work can be going fine, people can be nice to me—but most days I still feel pretty down, kind of empty. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to explain it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… it’s been a while. I think about two years now—maybe two years and a couple months. It kind of started after this dashboard project at work put me more in the spotlight. I don’t know if that sounds like a clear starting point, but that’s when I started noticing it more.
Do you find yourself enjoying activities or hobbies that you used to like before you started feeling this way?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I still do some things I used to like, so it’s not like I’ve stopped everything. I guess maybe they don’t always feel the same, but… I don’t know, maybe that’s normal? Like, I don’t want to overstate it.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t know if I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly. Like, I still do some of the same things, and I can get myself to go along with stuff. It just maybe feels a little less… rewarding? But I’m not sure if that counts, or if I’m making too much of it.
Do you feel like you're able to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you happiness?

I think… yes, at least sometimes. Like, if something is supposed to be fun, I can usually recognize that it’s nice, and I don’t want to make it sound like nothing feels good anymore. It’s just maybe not as strong as I’d expect? I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer do?

I’m not sure I can point to a specific thing and say, “I used to love that and now I don’t.” It’s more like… some things feel a little flatter than they used to, maybe. But I still can enjoy things at least somewhat, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you feel like you've lost pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, even if you still participate in them?

Maybe a little, but I’m not totally sure I’d call it “lost pleasure.” I still show up and do things, and sometimes they’re okay. It’s more like I’m going through the motions a bit, or the enjoyment is kind of muted. But I don’t want to overstate it if that’s not what you mean.
Do you feel like there are things that you do where you expect to feel happy, but the happiness isn't as strong as you think it should be?

Yeah… I think that’s probably a fair way to put it. Like, I’ll expect something to feel really good, and then when I’m there it’s just… fine. Not bad, exactly, just not as satisfying as I thought it would be. I still do feel some happiness sometimes, so I don’t want to make it sound like it’s completely gone. But maybe it’s a little weaker than it should be, if that makes sense.
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt completely back to normal for at least a couple of months?

Not really, no. I mean, there might have been better stretches here and there, but I don’t think I’ve had a full couple of months where I felt completely back to normal. It’s been kind of ongoing for about two years… maybe a little over, like two years and two months, since that dashboard project at work put me more in the spotlight. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past two years?
Not really, no. I mean, my weight probably goes up or down a little like anyone’s, but I haven’t noticed anything significant over the past couple years. At least nothing that stood out to me.
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt really down or depressed, almost every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days I’ve had this kind of flat, heavy feeling. Like even when work is going okay, or people are being nice to me, I still feel down or kind of empty underneath. That’s a big part of why I came in, actually.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

I’m not sure I’d call it anxious, exactly. I mean, I do worry about things sometimes, like anyone would, but I haven’t really noticed it being the main issue or anything. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt really down or depressed for two weeks or more in a row?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s fair to say. I don’t know if I’ve been counting it in two-week chunks exactly, but for a long time now I’ve had this flat, heavy feeling most days. Even when work is fine or people are nice to me, I still feel kind of down and empty underneath. That’s really why I came in.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get started on things than you used to?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still get things done, so I don’t want to overstate it, but by the afternoon I’m just wiped out. Even small stuff, like fixing an error in a spreadsheet or finishing expense paperwork, feels like I’m dragging my brain and my body through mud. Even getting myself to soccer can feel like a lot. Does that count as what you mean?
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt completely back to normal for at least two months in a row?

Not really, no. I mean, there have been better weeks, and I can function okay, but I don’t think I’ve had a full two months where I felt completely back to normal. This has been going on for about two years and a couple months, since that dashboard project at work kind of put me in the spotlight. Does that make sense?
Have you had more than one period in the last two years where you felt really down or depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if I’d separate it into clear “periods,” exactly. It’s more like I’ve been walking around with this flat, heavy feeling most days for a long time. Even when work is going okay or people are being nice, I still feel down and kind of empty underneath. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I can get in my head or misread a noise or something, but I’ve never heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t. At least not that I’m aware of.
Have you ever had thoughts that you think aren't your own or that are out of control?

I don’t think so… not in the sense that they feel like someone else put them there or anything. My thoughts can feel kind of repetitive or hard to shut off sometimes, but they still feel like mine, if that makes sense. Is that what you mean?
Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you felt really down or depressed, and if so, did they recur?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d mark them off as neat two-week stretches, but yes, I’ve felt really down for longer than that. It’s kind of the main reason I came in. For a long time now I’ve had this flat, heavy feeling most days—like even if work is fine or people are nice to me, I still feel down and kind of empty underneath. I’m not sure if that answers it the right way.
Have you had more than one distinct period of feeling really down or depressed over the past two years?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like it fully went away and then came back in clean episodes, exactly. It’s been more kind of ongoing for about two years and a couple months now, since that dashboard project at work put me more in the spotlight. There have been worse stretches in there, but mostly it’s just been… there. Does that count as more than one period?
